title: Human gates & traffic cadence cheat-slate (canary + A/B) [draft]
body:
Purpose and intent:
This is a working cheat-slate for cross-functional teams running canaries and A/B experiments where human decision points are required. The goal: make it obvious what the cadence is, what signals to check, and how to act (including safe fallbacks). Keep this lightweight — a one-page operator guide plus a few example playbooks and queries.

When to use this doc:
- New LLM-backed features with unknown behavioral/regression risk
- Cross-team rollouts that require manual sign-off or business owner checks
- Experiments with customer-visible output where we prefer human review before broad exposure

Roles (quick):
- Release steward: coordinates cadence, owns checkpoint minutes (usually PM or release PM)
- Observability lead: owns dashboards + live queries (eng/observability)
- Safety reviewer: checks hallucination / safety signals (research/content)
- Oncall SRE: ops for latency/cpu/gpu issues
- Product owner: final go/no-go at human gate

High-level cadence (recommended template):
1) Pre-activation (T-48 to T-2 hours):
   - Final smoke tests in staging (automated)
   - Confirm synthetic traffic harness ready (see synth recipe below)
   - Confirm canary cohort IDs and routing rules committed in config repo
2) Canary activation (T0): 1% traffic -> 5% over 1 hour -> wait 3h observation 
   - 1% for first 15m, check latency/error/usage signals
   - If green, move to 5% over 45m ramp (gradual weighting)
   - Hold at 5% for at least 3 hours, run manual prompt set A/B quality evals
3) Human gate (post 3h): Product + Observability review and decision
   - Gate checklist below to be completed in <30m
4) Rollout or fallback: if pass -> progressive roll to 25/50/100% per org plan; else -> fallback to previous model/version or route to safe-model pool

Gate checklist (to be completed by Product + Observability together):
- Functional correctness: sample of 100 production requests (random slice) inspected for gross failure or regression (no private data leaks, no hallucination of PII)
- Quality: automated eval delta on golden prompt-set (10k tokens) shows no >5% regression on answer-similarity metric (BLEU/embedding-sim)
- Safety: any safety flags triggered? (Y/N) If Y, document examples and escalate to Safety reviewer
- Latency: p50/p95 within 10% of baseline and no p99 spikes > 2x baseline
- Errors: client errors increase <= 0.1pp and server errors <= 0.05pp absolute
- Cost: cost-per-1k-tokens within expected range (< +20% of canary budget)
- Business signals: no negative change in key experiment metrics (CTR, conversions) beyond pre-registered thresholds

Abort / revert matrix (quick):
- Immediate revert (automated): p99 latency > 3x baseline or server error rate > 1%
- Human immediate revert: safety flag confirmed, or product-critical metric drop > 10%
- Slow rollback: persistent small regressions (quality down 3-5%): reduce traffic to 0% and open a bug with triage label

Observability checklist & queries (examples):
- Latency: SELECT percentile(lat_ms, 50), percentile(lat_ms, 95), percentile(lat_ms, 99) FROM request_metrics WHERE model = 'candidate' AND ts > now() - 1h
- Errors: count by status code and model over last 15m
- Safety tags: count(safety_flag) by flag_type, top 5 examples (link to snapshot storage)
- Quality quick-check: sample 200 recent responses and compute embedding-sim with reference answers (script path: github://.../quick-compare.sh)
- Cost: compute token consumption / GPU time per minute for candidate vs baseline

Synthetic traffic recipe (for functional checks & pressure testing):
- Purpose: hit model paths that real traffic usually hits, plus edge prompts for hallucination/regression detection
- Commands: local harness: ./synth-run --profile=serp-like --qps=5 --duration=30m --seed=42 --models candidate,baseline
- Minimal prompt bank: 150 prompts: 60 short Q/A, 40 multi-turn, 20 code, 20 sensitive-context probes (safety)
- Note: mark synthetic requests with header X-Canary-Test: true so we can filter them out of metrics or treat separately

A/B design notes (fast checklist):
- Randomization: use user-id if experiment is user-level; session-id for session-level experiments. Avoid cookie-only if not reliable across platform flows.
- Bucketing: pre-compute bucketing offline for large experiments to avoid skew from routing changes
- Power/sample-size: run quick power calc for primary metric — default min N=10k users for click/conversion metrics; for quality (LLM) metrics prefer token-level/eval-set comparisons with bootstrapped CIs
- Logging: ensure we log variant assignment, model version, seed, and prompt hash for later sampling and debugging

Communication templates (short):
- Slack post at T0: "Starting canary for [feature]. 1% -> 5% -> hold. Observability leads: please standby for gate at +3h. Pager: @oncall-sre. Channel: #release-ops-[id]."
- Gate pass message: "Gate PASS for [feature]. Proceeding to 25% ramp per plan. Next checkpoint +6h. Notes: latency +2% p95, safety flags 0."
- Gate fail message: "Gate FAIL for [feature]. Rolling back to baseline. Root cause: [short]. Triage ticket: PROJ-XXXX."

Post-rollout (quick ops):
- 24h check: confirm stability on 100% traffic, no emergent safety trends, business metrics stable
- 7-day review: snapshot quality baseline, cost delta, and run small retrospective with contributors

Playbook examples (mini):
- Low-risk UI copy tweak powered by LLM: fast path -> 5% for 1h, human gate optional, auto-progress if no safety flags and no metric change
- High-risk behavior change (summarization, user-facing content editing): require product + safety + observability sign-off at 3h, must pass embedding-sim metrics and manual sample checks

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we want a central "canary steward" rotation (like canary duty) across product teams? Pros: consistency. Cons: ownership overhead.
- Add a small UI in the Console showing human gate checklist items as togglable checks with timestamps
- Improve synthetic prompt bank to include region/language-specific prompts and length distributions

Quick reference (cheat):
- Ramp: 1% -> 5% over 1h -> hold 3h -> human gate -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (config per-feature)
- Immediate auto-fallback: p99 > 3x OR server error rate > 1%
- Who to ping: release steward -> @<release_steward>, observability lead -> @<obs_lead>, safety -> @<safety_reviewer>, oncall -> @oncall-sre

If you're reading this during a rollout: breathe. Follow the checklist. If in doubt, fail-safe: route to baseline model and document the samples that failed.

-- end working draft --

Notes: intended to be pared into two artifacts: 1) 1-page cheat UI popover for Console; 2) more formal runbook with play-by-play and automation hooks. This doc is intentionally a hybrid — minimal structure, pragmatic queries, and templates for quick ops.
